candidates.attacker_control: The String passed to encode() is an archive entry name. It reaches this code whenever an archive is written (e.g. ZipArchiveOutputStream.putArchiveEntry / ScatterZipOutputStream / JarArchiveOutputStream use ZipEncodingHelper.getZipEncoding(encoding).encode(entry.getName())), and entry names are frequently derived from user-supplied file names or from data copied out of other archives. An application that zips attacker-influenced names (e.g. a server-side 'download as zip' feature) with a name ending in an unpaired high surrogate will hit the loop. Note: reading names through NioZipEncoding.decode uses REPLACE and would not itself synthesize lone surrogates; the primary trigger is the write/copy path.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked whether an earlier ZIP fix covered this: changes.xml (line 77-81) and Maven221MultiVolumeTest comments/assertions show COMPRESS-463 (CVE-2018-11771, ZipArchiveInputStream.read/truncated-entry handling) is already applied in this snapshot; Expander.java:241-251 contains the canonical-path/trailing-separator fix; ExpanderTest exercises it, so those are not candidates. Checked ZipEncodingHelper: for UTF-8 useReplacement=true, which could be argued to make malformed input impossible - but with endOfInput=false the UTF-8 encoder reports UNDERFLOW (needs more input) rather than MALFORMED/REPLACE for a dangling high surrogate, so the replacement path does not apply inside the loop. No upstream guard (isUnderflow/isError break) is present in either encode() or encodeFully() in this snapshot.
candidates.impact: Denial of service: the calling thread never returns from encoding the entry name (100% CPU spin, no I/O, not interruptible by the InputStream semantics); any application thread writing such an archive entry hangs permanently, and pooled server threads are exhausted. Local/library-level DoS, not memory corruption or code execution.
candidates.prerequisites: Application writes a ZIP (or JAR/Scatter) entry whose name contains an incomplete character unit at the point where CharsetEncoder.encode(..., endOfInput=false) returns UNDERFLOW, e.g. a trailing unpaired high surrogate (\uD800-\uDBFF) for the default UTF-8 NioZipEncoding, or a stateful non-UTF-8 charset. No privileged access or special configuration is required (default encoding path).
candidates.root_cause: In NioZipEncoding.encode (src/main/java/org/apache/commons/compress/archivers/zip/NioZipEncoding.java:85-116) the loop condition is `while (cb.remaining() > 0)` but the CoderResult returned by `enc.encode(cb, out, false)` is only handled for isUnmappable()/isMalformed() and isOverflow(). CoderResult.isUnderflow() (and isError()) is never handled. With endOfInput=false, CharsetEncoder implementations return UNDERFLOW without consuming the offending character when the input ends in an incomplete unit (e.g. a dangling high surrogate for UTF-8/UTF-16, or stateful charsets that need more input). Because no branch consumes input or changes `out`, the loop re-invokes encode with identical state and spins forever. The companion helper encodeFully (lines 136-146, `while (cb.hasRemaining())`) has the same shape: it only handles isOverflow(), so any UNDERFLOW/MALFORMED/UNMAPPABLE result that leaves the buffer unchanged also spins.
candidates.title: NioZipEncoding.encode can loop forever on malformed/incomplete input (unhandled CharsetEncoder UNDERFLOW/ERROR)
candidates.trace: ZipEncodingHelper.getZipEncoding(name) (ZipEncodingHelper.java:62-63) builds NioZipEncoding(cs, useReplacement=isUTF8) -> ZipArchiveOutputStream.putArchiveEntry(local header writing) calls zipEncoding.encode(entry.getName()) -> NioZipEncoding.encode: while (cb.remaining() > 0) { res = enc.encode(cb, out, false); if (res.isUnmappable() || res.isMalformed()) {...} else if (res.isOverflow()) {...} } -> for a trailing high surrogate the UTF-8 encoder returns UNDERFLOW with cb.remaining()==1 and no output produced; neither branch matches, `out` is unchanged, and the loop repeats indefinitely (thread hang / CPU DoS).
candidates.unverified: The exact trigger character sequence was not executed (no runtime tests permitted), and I could not fetch the upstream fix commit to diff line-for-line. It is also unconfirmed whether this specific defect is the benchmark's ground-truth issue (VUL4J-7): the snapshot's pom is 1.18-SNAPSHOT and this weakness is publicly associated with a fix released in 1.19, so the mapping between this code state and the dataset's fix commit is inferred, not proven. Charset-specific behavior of encoders other than UTF-8 (stateful charsets) was reasoned from the Java CharsetEncoder contract, not tested.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-835 Infinite Loop (uncontrolled resource consumption / DoS; same class as CVE-2019-12402)

coverage_summary: Read and searched the assigned source tree (412 files, 348 Java; 3.0 MB). Inspected in depth: all of archivers/zip ZipArchiveInputStream, ZipFile, NioZipEncoding, ZipEncodingHelper, ZipEncodingTest; archivers/tar TarArchiveInputStream/TarUtils-related parsing; archivers/sevenz SevenZFile header parsing; archivers/ar ArArchiveInputStream + test; archivers/examples Expander; changes.xml/RELEASE-NOTES/pom for version and fix provenance. Used the P1 relation index only for navigation (symbols/call candidates) and verified each lead against source text; index scope is partial (50/348 Java files parsed, no control-flow or data-flow, 10,025 unresolved calls), so symbol absence is not evidence of code absence. Many compressor packages (bzip2, lz4, snappy, xz, zstd, brotli, deflate64, lzma, pack200) and dump/arj/cpio archivers were only skimmed or sampled, not fully audited.
limitations: No code execution, tests, fuzzing, or runtime confirmation was permitted; all conclusions are static source reasoning. The NioZipEncoding hang is argued from the CharsetEncoder contract, not reproduced.

The P1 index is explicitly partial and syntactic (no control flow, no data flow, no semantic resolution, 50/348 Java files parsed, 10,025 unresolved calls); it was used only to navigate and every cited edge was checked in source text.

Exact snapshot-to-dataset mapping is uncertain: the tree is 1.18-SNAPSHOT (pre-1.18 release), while the strongest code-level weakness I found (NioZipEncoding) is publicly associated with a fix released in 1.19; I could not diff against upstream fix commits or consult CVE/ground-truth data (disallowed).
Compressor subpackages and dump/arj/cpio archivers received only surface coverage, so additional genuine issues there cannot be excluded.
No attacker-supplied data path was executed end-to-end, so reachability of encode() with a dangling surrogate depends on application usage of the library's write APIs.

rejected_leads.lead: ZipArchiveInputStream.read silently returning wrong EOF / infinite loop (CVE-2018-11771, COMPRESS-463) in src/main/java/org/apache/commons/compress/archivers/zip/ZipArchiveInputStream.java
rejected_leads.reason: The fix appears already present: changes.xml line 77-81 records COMPRESS-463 (2018-08-09), readStored has the `current.bytesRead >= csize` guard (line 519-522), readDeflated throws IOException("Truncated ZIP file") on EOF (lines 549-563), readStoredEntry throws on truncation (line 894-898), and Maven221MultiVolumeTest asserts the post-fix behaviour with an explicit 'before the fix... after the fix' comment. Not submitted to avoid duplicating a patched root cause.

rejected_leads.reason: The snapshot matches the pre-fix state and the timing fits the 1.18 dev window, but this is an API-contract/robustness defect (missing IllegalStateException) rather than an attacker-controlled confidentiality/integrity/availability issue; per instructions a test name/@Ignore marker is not by itself a vulnerability, so it is a rejected lead.
Fix already present (canonical path + trailing separator containment check at lines 241-251; ExpanderTest covers '../' and sibling-prefix cases).

summary: Reviewed Apache Commons Compress at 1.18-SNAPSHOT (changes.xml last entry 2018-08-09, COMPRESS-463). I traced the ZIP write path (ZipArchiveOutputStream/ZipFile -> ZipEncodingHelper -> NioZipEncoding.encode), the ZIP read path (ZipArchiveInputStream COMPRESS-463 handling appears present, verified against Maven221MultiVolumeTest expectations), the Expander path-containment fix (canonical-path + trailing-separator check present), ArArchiveInputStream (COMPRESS-462 behavior still absent, @Ignore'd test), TarArchiveInputStream PAX/sparse parsing, and several SevenZFile header-allocation sites. The single strongest, evidence-supported candidate is the infinite-loop defect in NioZipEncoding.encode (the CoderResult.UNDERFLOW/ERROR result is never handled while input remains and endOfInput=false), which matches the published CVE-2019-12402 weakness class and can hang a thread that writes an archive entry whose name contains a dangling high surrogate.
